title: Client disconnect sweep and partial-draft sanitizer
creator: Liam O'Neill
description: Users and SDKs still trigger partial generations when clients disconnect or hit network blips. Leftover ephemeral state (partial drafts, stale KV cache entries, held leases) increases memory pressure and complicates resumable sessions. This ticket defines a pragmatic sweep + sanitizer that safely reclaims partial generation artifacts while preserving resumability where possible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Partial-generation artifacts (ephemeral draft, resume token, lease) are removed within configured grace period after confirmed client disconnect/timeout
2) Resume-capable sessions remain resumable if the client reconnects within the grace period (no data loss in >= 95% of reconnect scenarios in unit/integration tests),
3) KV cache prefetched entries associated with the orphaned generation are reclaimed to free GPU RAM without affecting concurrent generations on same model variant
4) Operational metrics emitted: orphaned_generations_reclaimed, reclaim_latency_ms, resumed_after_reclaim_count
5) No regressions in streaming SLOs (p95 latency) observed during controlled rollout in staging
technical_notes: Design: introduce a 'sanitizer' actor in the generation coordinator that runs periodic sweeps and targeted preemption when soft-grace windows expire.
Lease model: retain current lease token approach; add explicit lease state transitions: ACTIVE -> QUIESCED -> RECLAIMABLE -> RECLAIMED.
Grace window: default 30s QUIESCED then 5m RECLAIMABLE before final RECLAIMED. Expose cluster-level and per-customer overrides.
KV cache rescue: before reclaiming KV slices, attempt to snapshot small resume prefix into a compact resume blob if resume_age < 2m to support client reconnection; else reclaim immediately.
Backpressure interaction: sanitizer must coordinate with backpressure controller to avoid evicting resources when system-wide memory pressure is high; prefer delayed reclaim and emit alert.
Compatibility: sanitizer will be a backward-compatible runtime component; no changes to SDK protocol required. Use an opt-in feature flag for initial rollout.

APIs/Telemetry: add admin-only endpoints to list quarantined/orphaned generations and force-reclaim for debugging. Add telemetry dimensions: model_variant, customer_id, cause (disconnect|timeout|abandon).

Safety: ensure function-call/ tool-invocation side-effects are already committed to durable storage (or marked non-idempotent) before reclamation. If tool-call in-flight, mark generation as 'pending-tool-finalizer' and skip reclaim until finalizer completes or timeout expires.
implementation_plan: Week 1: prototype sanitizer actor and lease state transitions; wire basic reclaim path to delete ephemeral drafts and free memory slots
Week 2: integrate snapshot-for-resume path and KV slice collection; add telemetry and admin listing endpoints
Week 3: add coordination with backpressure/memory pressure signals and implement per-customer grace overrides
Week 4: tests + staging canary behind feature flag; run fault-injection scenarios and reconnection harness
Week 5: rollout to production gradually (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on error budgets
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike completed — implemented a minimal sanitizer loop in local runtime. Verified ephemeral draft deletion and lease state transitions locally. (Evelyn)
2025-02-12: Design review with Priya Singh (PM) and Marco Alvarez (Design). PM asked for admin listing endpoint and opt-in flag for customers in Dedicated. Added to scope. (Liam)

2025-02-13: Discovered race between sanitizer and a hedged-retry path in the request router causing double-reclaim in rare cases. Mitigation: add token compare-and-set on lease state before reclaim. (Evelyn)
2025-02-15: Added small resume snapshot logic; unit tests for resume within 90s passing. Filed follow-up ENG-776544 for stress test harness. (Evelyn)
2025-02-18: Integrated basic telemetry (orphaned_generations_reclaimed counter) into metrics pipeline; dashboards PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412).
risks: Accidental reclamation of an active session due to network partition — mitigated by two-step QUIESCED state and atomic lease CAS
Reclaiming KV slices could cause cold-start latency for concurrent generations on the same model variant if eviction is too aggressive
Tool/function-call in-flight: if not finalised, could lead to inconsistent side-effects. We gate reclaim on tool-finalizer complete or explicit timeout.
Operational complexity: new admin endpoints increase attack surface — require RBAC and audit logging
test_plan: Unit tests: lease transition state machine, sanitizer CAS logic, resume-snapshot creation and restore path
Integration tests: simulated client disconnects at different timings (immediate, 10s, 45s, 3m) and verify resumability or reclamation
Stress tests: run 10k short-lived streaming sessions with random disconnects and validate memory usage and reclaim throughput
Chaos tests: partition router while sanitizer runs to ensure no double-reclaim or lost resume tokens
E2E with SDKs: verify Node/Python SDK reconnection semantics unchanged
rollout_plan: Feature flag default=false. Stage 1: enable for internal staging cluster and Dedicated customers opted-in
Stage 2: Canary on 10% of hosted requests with increased telemetry sampling
Stage 3: Expand to 50% after 48h no regressions in SLOs, then full rollout after 7 days
Rollback: automated kill-switch on metric threshold breach (reclaim_errors > 0.5% or resumed_after_reclaim_count drops)
owner_notes: Keep initial reclaim conservative. Prioritize correctness and observability over aggressive memory savings. Coordinate with runtime infra team for KV metrics before broad rollout.
